paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: what you can see is not the whole picture. Elisha's servant got up early, went outside, and saw an army with horses and chariots all around the city. Elisha told him, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them." (2 Kings 6:16) Then the LORD opened the young man's eyes, and he saw "horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha." (2 Kings 6:17)

So when the bills pile up, or the news is loud, or the whole day looks like it surrounded you overnight, remember that servant. The problem was real, but it was never the biggest thing there. I'm LOUD about this because I've sat in the dark at the back of a drawer, sure that was the whole story. It wasn't. Ask the LORD to open your eyes, the same way Elisha asked for his servant. (2 Kings 6:17)

And look at what Elisha does with all that power on his side. He doesn't wipe out the men who came to capture him. He tells the king to set food and water before them, and the king prepares a great feast. (2 Kings 6:22-23) The text says the Aramean raiders did not come into the land of Israel again. (2 Kings 6:23) Friend, being on the winning side doesn't mean getting even. It means you've got room to be kind, even to someone who came after you.
